Try testing these in the \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e repository!\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eInteractive Sandboxes\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-interactive-sandboxes\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Interactive Sandboxes\" href=\"#interactive-sandboxes\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eStart up sandbox with an interactive shell so you can work interactively with a coding agent. This is similar to a git worktrees workflow, but provides stronger isolation. \u003ccode\u003eclaude\u003c/code\u003e is the default coding agent, but you can also specify \u003ccode\u003e--agent codex\u003c/code\u003e to use \u003ccode\u003ecodex\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"tsk shell\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003etsk shell\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003etsk shell\u003c/code\u003e command will:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eMake a copy of your repo\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eCreate a new git branch for you to work on\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eStart a proxy to limit internet access\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eBuild and start a container with your stack (go, python, rust, etc.) and agent (default: claude) installed\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eDrop you into an interactive shell\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAfter you exit the interactive shell (ctrl-d or \u003ccode\u003eexit\u003c/code\u003e), \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e will save any work you've done as a new branch in your original repo.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis workflow is really powerful when used with terminal multiplexers like \u003ccode\u003etmux\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003ezellij\u003c/code\u003e. It allows you to start multiple agents that are working on completely isolated copies of your repository with no opportunity to interfere with each other or access resources outside of the container.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eOne-off Fully Autonomous Agent Sandboxes\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-one-off-fully-autonomous-agent-sandboxes\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: One-off Fully Autonomous Agent Sandboxes\" href=\"#one-off-fully-autonomous-agent-sandboxes\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e has flags that help you avoid repetitive instructions like \"make sure unit tests pass\", \"update documentation\", or \"write a descriptive commit message\". Consider this command which immediately kicks off an autonomous agent in a sandbox to implement a new feature:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"tsk run --type feat --name greeting --prompt \u0026quot;Add a greeting to all tsk commands.\u0026quot;\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003etsk run --type feat --name greeting --prompt \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003eAdd a greeting to all tsk commands.\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSome important parts of the command:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--type\u003c/code\u003e specifies the type of task the agent is working on. Using \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e built-in tasks or writing your own can save a lot of boilerplate. Check out \u003ca href=\"/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/templates/feat.md\"\u003efeat.md\u003c/a\u003e for the \u003ccode\u003efeat\u003c/code\u003e type and \u003ca href=\"/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/templates\"\u003etemplates\u003c/a\u003e for all task types.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--name\u003c/code\u003e will be used in the final git branch to help you remember what task the branch contains.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--prompt\u003c/code\u003e is used to fill in the \u003ccode\u003e{{PROMPT}}\u003c/code\u003e placeholder in \u003ca href=\"/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/templates/feat.md\"\u003efeat.md\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSimilar to \u003ccode\u003etsk shell\u003c/code\u003e, the agent will run in a sandbox so it will not interfere with any ongoing work and will create a new branch in your repository in the background once it is done working.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAdd \u003ccode\u003e--branch main\u003c/code\u003e to start from a specific branch's committed state instead of your current working tree. This is useful when you want to launch a task from a different branch without switching to it.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAfter you try this command out, try out these next steps:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAdd the \u003ccode\u003e--edit\u003c/code\u003e flag to edit the full prompt that is sent to the agent.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAdd a custom task type. Use \u003ccode\u003etsk template list\u003c/code\u003e to see existing task templates and where you can add your own custom tasks.\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eSee the \u003ca href=\"/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/.tsk/templates\"\u003ecustom templates used by \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e for inspiration.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eQueuing Tasks for Parallel Execution\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-queuing-tasks-for-parallel-execution\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Queuing Tasks for Parallel Execution\" href=\"#queuing-tasks-for-parallel-execution\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e server allows you to have a single process that manages parallel task execution so you can easily background agents working. First, we start the server set up to handle up to 4 tasks in parallel:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"tsk server start --workers 4\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003etsk server start --workers 4\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eNow, in another terminal window, we can quickly queue up multiple tasks:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"# Add a task. Notice the similarity to the `tsk run` command\ntsk add --type doc --name tsk-architecture --prompt \u0026quot;Tell me how tsk works\u0026quot;\n\n# Look at the task queue. Your task `tsk-architecture` should be present in the list\ntsk list\n\n# Add another task. Notice the short flag names\ntsk add -t feat -n greeting -p \u0026quot;Add a silly robot greeting to every tsk command\u0026quot;\n\n# Now there should be two running tasks\ntsk list\n\n# Wait for a specific task to finish (blocks until complete)\ntsk wait \u0026lt;taskid\u0026gt;\n\n# Or look at all the branches after tasks complete\ngit branch --format=\u0026quot;%(refname:short) - %(subject) (%(committerdate:relative))\u0026quot;\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e Add a task. Notice the similarity to the `tsk run` command\u003c/span\u003e\ntsk add --type doc --name tsk-architecture --prompt \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003eTell me how tsk works\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\n\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e Look at the task queue. Your task `tsk-architecture` should be present in the list\u003c/span\u003e\ntsk list\n\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e Add another task. Notice the short flag names\u003c/span\u003e\ntsk add -t feat -n greeting -p \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003eAdd a silly robot greeting to every tsk command\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\n\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e Now there should be two running tasks\u003c/span\u003e\ntsk list\n\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e Wait for a specific task to finish (blocks until complete)\u003c/span\u003e\ntsk \u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003ewait\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026lt;\u003c/span\u003etaskid\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026gt;\u003c/span\u003e\n\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e Or look at all the branches after tasks complete\u003c/span\u003e\ngit branch --format=\u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e%(refname:short) - %(subject) (%(committerdate:relative))\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAfter you try this command out, try these next steps:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eUse \u003ccode\u003etsk add --wait\u003c/code\u003e to queue a task and block until it completes (useful in scripts and CI)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAdd tasks from multiple repositories in parallel\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eStart up multiple agents at once\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAdding \u003ccode\u003e--agent codex\u003c/code\u003e will use \u003ccode\u003ecodex\u003c/code\u003e to perform the task\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAdding \u003ccode\u003e--agent codex,claude\u003c/code\u003e will have \u003ccode\u003ecodex\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eclaude\u003c/code\u003e do the task in parallel with the same environment and instructions so you can compare agent performance\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAdding \u003ccode\u003e--agent claude,claude\u003c/code\u003e will have \u003ccode\u003eclaude\u003c/code\u003e do the task twice. This can be useful for exploratory changes to get ideas quickly\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eTask Chaining\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-task-chaining\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Task Chaining\" href=\"#task-chaining\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eChain tasks together with \u003ccode\u003e--parent\u003c/code\u003e so a child task starts from where its parent left off:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"# First task: set up the foundation\ntsk add -t feat -n add-api -p \u0026quot;Add a REST API endpoint for users\u0026quot;\n\n# Check the task list to get the task ID\ntsk list\n\n# Second task: chain it to the first (replace \u0026lt;taskid\u0026gt; with the parent's ID)\ntsk add -t feat -n add-tests -p \u0026quot;Add integration tests for the users API\u0026quot; --parent \u0026lt;taskid\u0026gt;\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e First task: set up the foundation\u003c/span\u003e\ntsk add -t feat -n add-api -p \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003eAdd a REST API endpoint for users\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\n\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e Check the task list to get the task ID\u003c/span\u003e\ntsk list\n\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e Second task: chain it to the first (replace \u0026lt;taskid\u0026gt; with the parent's ID)\u003c/span\u003e\ntsk add -t feat -n add-tests -p \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003eAdd integration tests for the users API\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e --parent \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026lt;\u003c/span\u003etaskid\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026gt;\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eChild tasks wait for their parent to complete, then start from the parent's final commit. \u003ccode\u003etsk list\u003c/code\u003e shows these tasks as \u003ccode\u003eWAITING\u003c/code\u003e. If a parent fails, its children are automatically marked as \u003ccode\u003eFAILED\u003c/code\u003e; if a parent is cancelled, its children are marked as \u003ccode\u003eCANCELLED\u003c/code\u003e. Chains of any length (A → B → C) are supported.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eCreate a Simple Task Template\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-create-a-simple-task-template\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Create a Simple Task Template\" href=\"#create-a-simple-task-template\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eLet's create a very basic way to automate working on GitHub issues:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"# First create the tsk template configuration directory\nmkdir -p ~/.config/tsk/templates\n\n# Create a very simple template. Notice the use of the \u0026quot;{{PROMPT}}\u0026quot; placeholder\ncat \u0026gt; ~/.config/tsk/templates/issue-bot.md \u0026lt;\u0026lt; 'EOF'\nSolve the GitHub issue below. Make sure it is tested and write a descriptive commit\nmessage describing the changes after you are done.\n\n{{PROMPT}}\nEOF\n\n# Make sure tsk sees the new `issue-bot` task template\ntsk template list\n\n# Pipe in some input to start the task\n# Piped input automatically replaces the {{PROMPT}} placeholder\ngh issue view \u0026lt;issue-number\u0026gt; | tsk add -t issue-bot -n fix-my-issue\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e First create the tsk template configuration directory\u003c/span\u003e\nmkdir -p \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e~\u003c/span\u003e/.config/tsk/templates\n\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e Create a very simple template. Notice the use of the \"{{PROMPT}}\" placeholder\u003c/span\u003e\ncat \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026gt;\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e~\u003c/span\u003e/.config/tsk/templates/issue-bot.md \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026lt;\u0026lt;\u003c/span\u003e '\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eEOF\u003c/span\u003e'\u003c/span\u003e\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003eSolve the GitHub issue below. data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"# Container engine (top-level setting, user-only)\ncontainer_engine = \u0026quot;docker\u0026quot;  # \u0026quot;docker\u0026quot; (default) or \u0026quot;podman\u0026quot;\n\n# Server daemon configuration (user-only)\n[server]\nauto_clean_enabled = true   # Automatically clean old tasks (default: true)\nauto_clean_age_days = 7.0   # Minimum age in days before cleanup (default: 7.0)\n\n# Default settings for all projects (showing built-in defaults)\n[defaults]\nagent = \u0026quot;claude\u0026quot;             # AI agent: \u0026quot;claude\u0026quot; or \u0026quot;codex\u0026quot;\nstack = \u0026quot;default\u0026quot;            # Tech stack (auto-detected from project files)\nmemory_gb = 12.0             # Container memory limit in GB\ncpu = 8                      # Number of CPUs\ndind = false                 # Enable Docker-in-Docker support\nprivileged = false           # Run containers in privileged mode (disables security restrictions)\nsudo = false                 # Enable passwordless sudo inside containers\ndevices = []                 # Device paths to expose (e.g., [\u0026quot;/dev/video0\u0026quot;])\ngit_town = false             # Enable git-town parent branch tracking\n\n# Project-specific overrides (matches directory name)\n[project.my-go-service]\nstack = \u0026quot;go\u0026quot;\nmemory_gb = 24.0\ncpu = 16\nsetup = '''\nUSER root\nRUN apt-get update \u0026amp;\u0026amp; apt-get install -y libssl-dev pkg-config\nUSER agent\n'''\nhost_ports = [5432, 6379]    # Forward host ports to containers\nvolumes = [\n    # Bind mount: share host directories with containers (supports ~ expansion)\n    { host = \u0026quot;~/.cache/go-mod\u0026quot;, container \u003ccode\u003esetup\u003c/code\u003e field injects Dockerfile commands at the project layer position in the Docker image build. Use it for project-specific build dependencies. \u003ccode\u003estack_config.\u0026lt;name\u0026gt;.setup\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eagent_config.\u0026lt;name\u0026gt;.setup\u003c/code\u003e similarly inject content at the stack and agent layer positions, and can define entirely new stacks or agents (e.g., \u003ccode\u003estack_config.scala.setup\u003c/code\u003e lets you use \u003ccode\u003estack = \"scala\"\u003c/code\u003e). Config-defined layers take priority over embedded Docker layers. Setup commands run as the \u003ccode\u003eagent\u003c/code\u003e user by default — use \u003ccode\u003eUSER root\u003c/code\u003e for operations that require elevated privileges (e.g., \u003ccode\u003eapt-get install\u003c/code\u003e) and always switch back to \u003ccode\u003eUSER agent\u003c/code\u003e afterwards.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eVolume mounts are particularly useful for:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBuild caches\u003c/strong\u003e: Share Go module cache (\u003ccode\u003e/go/pkg/mod\u003c/code\u003e) or Rust target directories to speed up builds\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePersistent state\u003c/strong\u003e: Use named volumes for build caches that persist across tasks\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRead-only artifacts\u003c/strong\u003e: Mount debugging artifacts, config files, or other resources without risk of modification\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEnvironment variables (\u003ccode\u003eenv\u003c/code\u003e) let you pass configuration to task containers, such as database URLs or API keys. To connect to host services forwarded through the proxy, use the \u003ccode\u003eTSK_PROXY_HOST\u003c/code\u003e environment variable (set automatically by \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e) as the hostname.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe container engine can also be set per-command with the \u003ccode\u003e--container-engine\u003c/code\u003e flag (available on \u003ccode\u003erun\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eshell\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eretry\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecancel\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eserver start\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003edocker build\u003c/code\u003e).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eHost ports (\u003ccode\u003ehost_ports\u003c/code\u003e) expose host services to task containers. Agents connect to \u003ccode\u003e$TSK_PROXY_HOST:\u0026lt;port\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e to reach services running on your host machine (e.g., local databases or dev servers). The \u003ccode\u003eTSK_PROXY_HOST\u003c/code\u003e environment variable is automatically set by \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e to the correct proxy container hostname.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhen \u003ccode\u003egit_town\u003c/code\u003e is enabled, \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e integrates with \u003ca href=\"https://www.git-town.com/\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003egit-town\u003c/a\u003e by setting the parent branch metadata on task branches, allowing git-town commands like \u003ccode\u003egit town sync\u003c/code\u003e to work correctly with \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e-created branches.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eConfiguration priority: CLI flags \u0026gt; user \u003ccode\u003e[project.\u0026lt;name\u0026gt;]\u003c/code\u003e \u0026gt; project \u003ccode\u003e.tsk/tsk.toml\u003c/code\u003e \u0026gt; user \u003ccode\u003e[defaults]\u003c/code\u003e \u0026gt; auto-detection \u0026gt; built-in defaults\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSettings in \u003ccode\u003e[defaults]\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e[project.\u0026lt;name\u0026gt;]\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003e.tsk/tsk.toml\u003c/code\u003e share the same shape. Scalars use first-set in priority order. Lists (\u003ccode\u003evolumes\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eenv\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ehost_ports\u003c/code\u003e) combine across layers, with higher-priority winning on conflicts (same container path, same env var name, same port). \u003ccode\u003estack_config\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003eagent_config\u003c/code\u003e maps combine all names; for the same name, higher-priority replaces the entire config.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eCustomizing the \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e Sandbox Environment\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-customizing-the-tsk-sandbox-environment\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Customizing the tsk Sandbox Environment\" href=\"#customizing-the-tsk-sandbox-environment\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEach \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e sandbox container image has 4 main parts:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eA \u003ca href=\"/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/dockerfiles/base/default.dockerfile\"\u003ebase dockerfile\u003c/a\u003e that includes the OS and a set of basic development tools e.g. \u003ccode\u003egit\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003egit-lfs\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eA \u003ccode\u003estack\u003c/code\u003e snippet that defines language specific build steps. See:\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/dockerfiles/stack/default.dockerfile\"\u003edefault\u003c/a\u003e - minimal fallback stack\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/dockerfiles/stack/go.dockerfile\"\u003ego\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/dockerfiles/stack/java.dockerfile\"\u003ejava\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/dockerfiles/stack/lua.dockerfile\"\u003elua\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/dockerfiles/stack/node.dockerfile\"\u003enode\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/dockerfiles/stack/python.dockerfile\"\u003epython\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/dockerfiles/stack/rust.dockerfile\"\u003erust\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAn \u003ccode\u003eagent\u003c/code\u003e snippet that installs an agent, e.g. \u003ccode\u003eclaude\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003ecodex\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eA \u003ccode\u003eproject\u003c/code\u003e snippet that defines project specific build steps (applied last for project-specific customizations). This does nothing by default, but can be used to add extra build steps for your project.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIt is very difficult to make these images general purpose enough to cover all repositories. You may need some special customization. If you use Claude Code, the \u003ccode\u003etsk-config\u003c/code\u003e skill can walk you through configuring \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e's Docker layers for your project (see \u003ca href=\"#claude-code-skills-marketplace\"\u003eClaude Code Skills Marketplace\u003c/a\u003e for installation). Otherwise, the recommended approach is to use \u003ccode\u003esetup\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003estack_config\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003eagent_config\u003c/code\u003e fields in your \u003ccode\u003etsk.toml\u003c/code\u003e to inject custom Dockerfile commands (see \u003ca href=\"#configuration-file\"\u003eConfiguration File\u003c/a\u003e above).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSee \u003ca href=\"/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/dockerfiles\"\u003edockerfiles\u003c/a\u003e for the built-in dockerfiles.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eYou can run \u003ccode\u003etsk docker build --dry-run\u003c/code\u003e to see the dockerfile that \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e will dynamically generate for your repository.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSee the \u003ca href=\"/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/docs/docker-builds.md\"\u003eDocker Builds Guide\u003c/a\u003e for a more in-depth walk through, and the \u003ca href=\"/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/docs/network-isolation.md\"\u003eNetwork Isolation Guide\u003c/a\u003e for details on how \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e secures agent network access.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eI'm working on improving this part of \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e to be as seamless and easy to set up as possible, but it's still a work in progress. I welcome all feedback on how to make this easier and more intuitive!\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eCreating Templates\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-creating-templates\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Creating Templates\" href=\"#creating-templates\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTemplates are simply markdown files that get passed to agents. \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e additionally adds a convenience \u003ccode\u003e{{PROMPT}}\u003c/code\u003e placeholder that will get replaced by anything you pipe into tsk or pass in via the \u003ccode\u003e-p/--prompt\u003c/code\u003e flag, or by using \u003ccode\u003e--prompt-file \u0026lt;path\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e to read from a file. The legacy \u003ccode\u003e{{DESCRIPTION}}\u003c/code\u003e placeholder is still supported but deprecated.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTo inspect an existing template, run \u003ccode\u003etsk template show \u0026lt;template\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e. To customize a built-in template, run \u003ccode\u003etsk template edit \u0026lt;template\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e — \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e will copy it to \u003ccode\u003e~/.config/tsk/templates/\u003c/code\u003e and open it in your \u003ccode\u003e$EDITOR\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTo create good templates, I would recommend thinking about repetitive tasks that you need agents to do within your codebase like \"make sure the unit tests pass\", \"write a commit message\", etc. and encode those in a template file. There are many great prompting guides out there so I'll spare the details here.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eCustom Proxy Configuration\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-custom-proxy-configuration\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Custom Proxy Configuration\" href=\"#custom-proxy-configuration\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e uses Squid as a forward proxy to control network access from task containers. See the default \u003ca href=\"/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/dockerfiles/tsk-proxy/squid.conf\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e squid.conf\u003c/a\u003e as a starting point.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePer-configuration proxy instances:\u003c/strong\u003e Tasks with different proxy configurations (different \u003ccode\u003ehost_ports\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003esquid_conf\u003c/code\u003e) automatically get separate proxy containers. Tasks with identical proxy config share the same proxy. Proxy containers are named \u003ccode\u003etsk-proxy-{fingerprint}\u003c/code\u003e where the fingerprint is derived from the proxy configuration.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e Data Directory\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-tsk-data-directory\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: tsk Data Directory\" href=\"#tsk-data-directory\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e uses the following directories for storing data while running tasks:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e~/.local/share/tsk/tasks.db\u003c/strong\u003e: SQLite database for task queue and task definitions\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e~/.local/share/tsk/tasks/\u003c/strong\u003e: Task directories that get mounted into sandboxes when the agent runs. They contain:\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e/repo\u003c/strong\u003e: The repo copy that the agent operates on\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e/output\u003c/strong\u003e: Directory containing \u003ccode\u003eagent.log\u003c/code\u003e with structured JSON-lines output including infrastructure phases (image build, agent launch, saving changes, branch result) and processed agent output\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e/instructions.md\u003c/strong\u003e: The instructions that were passed to an agent\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThese default paths follow XDG conventions. You can override them with \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e-specific environment variables without affecting other XDG-aware software. Like XDG variables, these specify the base directory; \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e appends \u003ccode\u003e/tsk\u003c/code\u003e automatically:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003eTSK_DATA_HOME\u003c/code\u003e - overrides \u003ccode\u003eXDG_DATA_HOME\u003c/code\u003e for \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e (default: \u003ccode\u003e~/.local/share\u003c/code\u003e)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003eTSK_RUNTIME_DIR\u003c/code\u003e - overrides \u003ccode\u003eXDG_RUNTIME_DIR\u003c/code\u003e for \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e (default: \u003ccode\u003e/tmp\u003c/code\u003e)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003eTSK_CONFIG_HOME\u003c/code\u003e - overrides \u003ccode\u003eXDG_CONFIG_HOME\u003c/code\u003e for \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e (default: \u003ccode\u003e~/.config\u003c/code\u003e)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eClaude Code Skills Marketplace\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-claude-code-skills-marketplace\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Claude Code Skills Marketplace\" href=\"#claude-code-skills-marketplace\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis repository includes a Claude Code skills marketplace with \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e-specific skills that teach Claude how to use \u003ccode\u003etsk\u003c/code\u003e commands. <p dir="auto">Delegate development <code>tsk</code> tasks to YOLO mode AI agents running in sandbox containers. <code>tsk</code> auto-detects your toolchain and builds container images for you, so most projects require very little setup. Agents work asynchronously and in parallel so you can review their work on your own schedule, respecting your time and attention.</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li><strong>Assign tasks</strong> using templates that automate prompt boilerplate</li>
<li><strong><code>tsk</code> copies your repo</strong> and builds containers with your toolchain automatically</li>
<li><strong>Agents work in YOLO mode</strong> in parallel filesystem and network isolated containers</li>
<li><strong><code>tsk</code> fetches branches</strong> back to your repo for review</li>
<li><strong>Review and merge</strong> on your own schedule</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Each agent gets what it needs and nothing more:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Agent configuration (e.g. <code>~/.claude</code> or <code>~/.codex</code>)</li>
<li>A copy of your repo excluding gitignored files (no accidental API key sharing)</li>
<li>An isolated filesystem (no accidental <code>rm -rf .git</code>)</li>
<li>A configurable domain allowlist (Agents can't share your code on MoltBook)</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Each agent runs in an isolated network where all traffic routes through a proxy sidecar, enforcing the domain allowlist. Beyond network restrictions, agents have full control within their container.</p>
<p dir="auto">Supports Claude Code and Codex coding agents. Docker and Podman container runtimes.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Quick Start Guide</h2><a id="user-content-quick-start-guide" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Quick Start Guide" href="#quick-start-guide"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>tsk</code> can be used in multiple ways. Here are some of the main workflows to get started. Try testing these in the <code>tsk</code> repository!</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Interactive Sandboxes</h3><a id="user-content-interactive-sandboxes" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Interactive Sandboxes" href="#interactive-sandboxes"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Start up sandbox with an interactive shell so you can work interactively with a coding agent. This is similar to a git worktrees workflow, but provides stronger isolation. <code>claude</code> is the default coding agent, but you can also specify <code>--agent codex</code> to use <code>codex</code>.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="tsk shell"><pre>tsk shell</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The <code>tsk shell</code> command will:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Make a copy of your repo</li>
<li>Create a new git branch for you to work on</li>
<li>Start a proxy to limit internet access</li>
<li>Build and start a container with your stack (go, python, rust, etc.) and agent (default: claude) installed</li>
<li>Drop you into an interactive shell</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">After you exit the interactive shell (ctrl-d or <code>exit</code>), <code>tsk</code> will save any work you've done as a new branch in your original repo.</p>
<p dir="auto">This workflow is really powerful when used with terminal multiplexers like <code>tmux</code> or <code>zellij</code>. It allows you to start multiple agents that are working on completely isolated copies of your repository with no opportunity to interfere with each other or access resources outside of the container.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">One-off Fully Autonomous Agent Sandboxes</h3><a id="user-content-one-off-fully-autonomous-agent-sandboxes" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: One-off Fully Autonomous Agent Sandboxes" href="#one-off-fully-autonomous-agent-sandboxes"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>tsk</code> has flags that help you avoid repetitive instructions like "make sure unit tests pass", "update documentation", or "write a descriptive commit message". Consider this command which immediately kicks off an autonomous agent in a sandbox to implement a new feature:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="tsk run --type feat --name greeting --prompt "Add a greeting to all tsk commands.""><pre>tsk run --type feat --name greeting --prompt <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Add a greeting to all tsk commands.<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Some important parts of the command:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>--type</code> specifies the type of task the agent is working on. Using <code>tsk</code> built-in tasks or writing your own can save a lot of boilerplate. Check out <a href="/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/templates/feat.md">feat.md</a> for the <code>feat</code> type and <a href="/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/templates">templates</a> for all task types.</li>
<li><code>--name</code> will be used in the final git branch to help you remember what task the branch contains.</li>
<li><code>--prompt</code> is used to fill in the <code>{{PROMPT}}</code> placeholder in <a href="/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/templates/feat.md">feat.md</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Similar to <code>tsk shell</code>, the agent will run in a sandbox so it will not interfere with any ongoing work and will create a new branch in your repository in the background once it is done working.</p>
<p dir="auto">Add <code>--branch main</code> to start from a specific branch's committed state instead of your current working tree. This is useful when you want to launch a task from a different branch without switching to it.</p>
<p dir="auto">After you try this command out, try out these next steps:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Add the <code>--edit</code> flag to edit the full prompt that is sent to the agent.</li>
<li>Add a custom task type. Use <code>tsk template list</code> to see existing task templates and where you can add your own custom tasks.
<ul dir="auto">
<li>See the <a href="/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/.tsk/templates">custom templates used by <code>tsk</code></a> for inspiration.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Queuing Tasks for Parallel Execution</h3><a id="user-content-queuing-tasks-for-parallel-execution" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Queuing Tasks for Parallel Execution" href="#queuing-tasks-for-parallel-execution"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The <code>tsk</code> server allows you to have a single process that manages parallel task execution so you can easily background agents working. First, we start the server set up to handle up to 4 tasks in parallel:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="tsk server start --workers 4"><pre>tsk server start --workers 4</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Now, in another terminal window, we can quickly queue up multiple tasks:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="# Add a task. Notice the similarity to the `tsk run` command
tsk add --type doc --name tsk-architecture --prompt "Tell me how tsk works"

# Look at the task queue. Your task `tsk-architecture` should be present in the list
tsk list

# Add another task. Notice the short flag names
tsk add -t feat -n greeting -p "Add a silly robot greeting to every tsk command"

# Now there should be two running tasks
tsk list

# Wait for a specific task to finish (blocks until complete)
tsk wait <taskid>

# Or look at all the branches after tasks complete
git branch --format="%(refname:short) - %(subject) (%(committerdate:relative))""><pre><span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Add a task. Notice the similarity to the `tsk run` command</span>
tsk add --type doc --name tsk-architecture --prompt <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Tell me how tsk works<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Look at the task queue. Your task `tsk-architecture` should be present in the list</span>
tsk list

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Add another task. Notice the short flag names</span>
tsk add -t feat -n greeting -p <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Add a silly robot greeting to every tsk command<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Now there should be two running tasks</span>
tsk list

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Wait for a specific task to finish (blocks until complete)</span>
tsk <span class="pl-c1">wait</span> <span class="pl-k"><</span>taskid<span class="pl-k">></span>

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Or look at all the branches after tasks complete</span>
git branch --format=<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>%(refname:short) - %(subject) (%(committerdate:relative))<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">After you try this command out, try these next steps:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Use <code>tsk add --wait</code> to queue a task and block until it completes (useful in scripts and CI)</li>
<li>Add tasks from multiple repositories in parallel</li>
<li>Start up multiple agents at once
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Adding <code>--agent codex</code> will use <code>codex</code> to perform the task</li>
<li>Adding <code>--agent codex,claude</code> will have <code>codex</code> and <code>claude</code> do the task in parallel with the same environment and instructions so you can compare agent performance</li>
<li>Adding <code>--agent claude,claude</code> will have <code>claude</code> do the task twice. This can be useful for exploratory changes to get ideas quickly</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Task Chaining</h3><a id="user-content-task-chaining" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Task Chaining" href="#task-chaining"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Chain tasks together with <code>--parent</code> so a child task starts from where its parent left off:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="# First task: set up the foundation
tsk add -t feat -n add-api -p "Add a REST API endpoint for users"

# Check the task list to get the task ID
tsk list

# Second task: chain it to the first (replace <taskid> with the parent's ID)
tsk add -t feat -n add-tests -p "Add integration tests for the users API" --parent <taskid>"><pre><span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> First task: set up the foundation</span>
tsk add -t feat -n add-api -p <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Add a REST API endpoint for users<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Check the task list to get the task ID</span>
tsk list

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Second task: chain it to the first (replace <taskid> with the parent's ID)</span>
tsk add -t feat -n add-tests -p <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Add integration tests for the users API<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> --parent <span class="pl-k"><</span>taskid<span class="pl-k">></span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Child tasks wait for their parent to complete, then start from the parent's final commit. <code>tsk list</code> shows these tasks as <code>WAITING</code>. If a parent fails, its children are automatically marked as <code>FAILED</code>; if a parent is cancelled, its children are marked as <code>CANCELLED</code>. Chains of any length (A → B → C) are supported.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Create a Simple Task Template</h3><a id="user-content-create-a-simple-task-template" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Create a Simple Task Template" href="#create-a-simple-task-template"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Let's create a very basic way to automate working on GitHub issues:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="# First create the tsk template configuration directory
mkdir -p ~/.config/tsk/templates

# Create a very simple template. Notice the use of the "{{PROMPT}}" placeholder
cat > ~/.config/tsk/templates/issue-bot.md << 'EOF'
Solve the GitHub issue below. Make sure it is tested and write a descriptive commit
message describing the changes after you are done.

{{PROMPT}}
EOF

# Make sure tsk sees the new `issue-bot` task template
tsk template list

# Pipe in some input to start the task
# Piped input automatically replaces the {{PROMPT}} placeholder
gh issue view <issue-number> | tsk add -t issue-bot -n fix-my-issue"><pre><span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> First create the tsk template configuration directory</span>
mkdir -p <span class="pl-k">~</span>/.config/tsk/templates

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Create a very simple template. Notice the use of the "{{PROMPT}}" placeholder</span>
cat <span class="pl-k">></span> <span class="pl-k">~</span>/.config/tsk/templates/issue-bot.md <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-k"><<</span> '<span class="pl-k">EOF</span>'</span>
<span class="pl-s">Solve the GitHub issue below. Make sure it is tested and write a descriptive commit</span>
<span class="pl-s">message describing the changes after you are done.</span>
<span class="pl-s"></span>
<span class="pl-s">{{PROMPT}}</span>
<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-k">EOF</span></span>

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Make sure tsk sees the new `issue-bot` task template</span>
tsk template list

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Pipe in some input to start the task</span>
<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Piped input automatically replaces the {{PROMPT}} placeholder</span>
gh issue view <span class="pl-k"><</span>issue-number<span class="pl-k">></span> <span class="pl-k">|</span> tsk add -t issue-bot -n fix-my-issue</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Now it's easy to solve GitHub issues with a simple task template. Try this with code reviews as well to easily respond to feedback.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Commands</h2><a id="user-content-commands" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Commands" href="#commands"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Task Commands</h3><a id="user-content-task-commands" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Task Commands" href="#task-commands"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Create, manage, and monitor tasks assigned to AI agents.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>tsk run</code> - Execute a task immediately (supports <code>--branch <branch></code> to start from a specific branch's HEAD; Ctrl+C marks task as CANCELLED)</li>
<li><code>tsk shell</code> - Start a sandbox container with an interactive shell (supports <code>--branch <branch></code> to start from a specific branch's HEAD)</li>
<li><code>tsk add</code> - Queue a task (supports <code>--parent <taskid></code> for task chaining, <code>--wait</code> to block until completion, <code>--branch <branch></code> to start from a specific branch's HEAD)</li>
<li><code>tsk list</code> - View task status and branches</li>
<li><code>tsk wait <task-id>...</code> - Block until one or more tasks complete (exits non-zero if any task failed, was cancelled, or is blocked by a warmup error)</li>
<li><code>tsk cancel <task-id>...</code> - Cancel one or more running or queued tasks</li>
<li><code>tsk clean</code> - Clean up completed tasks</li>
<li><code>tsk delete <task-id>...</code> - Delete one or more tasks</li>
<li><code>tsk retry <task-id>...</code> - Retry one or more tasks</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Server Commands</h3><a id="user-content-server-commands" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Server Commands" href="#server-commands"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Manage the <code>tsk</code> server daemon for parallel task execution. The server automatically cleans up completed, failed, and cancelled tasks older than 7 days.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>tsk server start</code> - Start the <code>tsk</code> server daemon</li>
<li><code>tsk server stop</code> - Stop the running <code>tsk</code> server</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Graceful shutdown (via <code>q</code>, Ctrl+C, or <code>tsk server stop</code>) marks any in-progress tasks as CANCELLED.</p>
<p dir="auto">When running in an interactive terminal, <code>tsk server start</code> shows a TUI dashboard with a split-pane view: task list on the left, log viewer on the right. In the task list, active tasks (Running, Queued, Waiting) appear above completed or failed tasks. The log viewer starts at the bottom of the selected task's output and auto-follows new content. Scrolling up pauses follow mode; scrolling back to the bottom resumes it. When stdout is piped or non-interactive (e.g. <code>tsk server start | cat</code>), plain text output is used instead.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>TUI Controls:</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>Left</code> / <code>h</code>: Focus the task list panel</li>
<li><code>Right</code> / <code>l</code>: Focus the log viewer panel</li>
<li><code>Up</code> / <code>k</code>, <code>Down</code> / <code>j</code>: Navigate tasks or scroll logs (depends on focused panel)</li>
<li><code>Page Up</code> / <code>Page Down</code>: Jump scroll in log viewer</li>
<li>Click: Select a task or focus a panel</li>
<li>Mouse scroll: scroll tasks or logs</li>
<li>Scrollbar click/drag: Jump or scrub through the task list</li>
<li><code>Shift+click</code> / <code>Shift+drag</code>: Select text (bypasses mouse capture for clipboard use)</li>
<li><code>c</code>: Cancel the selected task (when task panel is focused, only RUNNING/QUEUED tasks)</li>
<li><code>d</code>: Delete the selected task (when task panel is focused, only terminal-state tasks)</li>
<li><code>q</code>: Quit the server (graceful shutdown)</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Configuration Commands</h3><a id="user-content-configuration-commands" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Configuration Commands" href="#configuration-commands"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Build container images and manage task templates.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>tsk docker build</code> - Build required container images</li>
<li><code>tsk template list</code> - View available task type templates and where they are installed</li>
<li><code>tsk template show <template></code> - Display the contents of a template</li>
<li><code>tsk template edit <template></code> - Open a template in your editor for customization</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Run <code>tsk help</code> or <code>tsk help <command></code> for detailed options.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Configuring <code>tsk</code></h2><a id="user-content-configuring-tsk" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Configuring tsk" href="#configuring-tsk"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>tsk</code> has 3 levels of configuration in priority order:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Project level in the <code>.tsk</code> folder local to your project</li>
<li>User level in <code>~/.config/tsk</code></li>
<li>Built-in configurations</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Each configuration directory can contain:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>templates</code>: A folder of task template markdown files which can be used via the <code>-t/--type</code> flag</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Configuration File</h3><a id="user-content-configuration-file" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Configuration File" href="#configuration-file"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>tsk</code> can be configured at two levels:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li><strong>User-level</strong>: <code>~/.config/tsk/tsk.toml</code> — global settings, defaults, and per-project overrides</li>
<li><strong>Project-level</strong>: <code>.tsk/tsk.toml</code> in your project root — shared project defaults (checked into version control)</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Both levels use the same shared config shape. The project-level config only contains shared settings (no <code>container_engine</code>, <code>[server]</code>, or <code>[project.<name>]</code> sections).</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>User-level config</strong> (<code>~/.config/tsk/tsk.toml</code>):</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-toml notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="# Container engine (top-level setting, user-only)
container_engine = "docker"  # "docker" (default) or "podman"

# Server daemon configuration (user-only)
[server]
auto_clean_enabled = true   # Automatically clean old tasks (default: true)
auto_clean_age_days = 7.0   # Minimum age in days before cleanup (default: 7.0)

# Default settings for all projects (showing built-in defaults)
[defaults]
agent = "claude"             # AI agent: "claude" or "codex"
stack = "default"            # Tech stack (auto-detected from project files)
memory_gb = 12.0             # Container memory limit in GB
cpu = 8                      # Number of CPUs
dind = false                 # Enable Docker-in-Docker support
privileged = false           # Run containers in privileged mode (disables security restrictions)
sudo = false                 # Enable passwordless sudo inside containers
devices = []                 # Device paths to expose (e.g., ["/dev/video0"])
git_town = false             # Enable git-town parent branch tracking

# Project-specific overrides (matches directory name)
[project.my-go-service]
stack = "go"
memory_gb = 24.0
cpu = 16
setup = '''
USER root
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y libssl-dev pkg-config
USER agent
'''
host_ports = [5432, 6379]    # Forward host ports to containers
volumes = [
    # Bind mount: share host directories with containers (supports ~ expansion)
    { host = "~/.cache/go-mod", container = "/go/pkg/mod" },
    # Named volume: container-managed persistent storage (prefixed with tsk-)
    { name = "go-build-cache", container = "/home/agent/.cache/go-build" },
    # Read-only mount: provide artifacts without modification risk
    { host = "~/debug-logs", container = "/debug-logs", readonly = true }
]
env = [
    { name = "DB_PORT", value = "5432" },
    { name = "REDIS_PORT", value = "6379" },
]"><pre><span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Container engine (top-level setting, user-only)</span>

<p dir="auto">The <code>setup</code> field injects Dockerfile commands at the project layer position in the Docker image build. Use it for project-specific build dependencies. <code>stack_config.<name>.setup</code> and <code>agent_config.<name>.setup</code> similarly inject content at the stack and agent layer positions, and can define entirely new stacks or agents (e.g., <code>stack_config.scala.setup</code> lets you use <code>stack = "scala"</code>). Config-defined layers take priority over embedded Docker layers. Setup commands run as the <code>agent</code> user by default — use <code>USER root</code> for operations that require elevated privileges (e.g., <code>apt-get install</code>) and always switch back to <code>USER agent</code> afterwards.</p>
<p dir="auto">Volume mounts are particularly useful for:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Build caches</strong>: Share Go module cache (<code>/go/pkg/mod</code>) or Rust target directories to speed up builds</li>
<li><strong>Persistent state</strong>: Use named volumes for build caches that persist across tasks</li>
<li><strong>Read-only artifacts</strong>: Mount debugging artifacts, config files, or other resources without risk of modification</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Environment variables (<code>env</code>) let you pass configuration to task containers, such as database URLs or API keys. To connect to host services forwarded through the proxy, use the <code>TSK_PROXY_HOST</code> environment variable (set automatically by <code>tsk</code>) as the hostname.</p>
<p dir="auto">The container engine can also be set per-command with the <code>--container-engine</code> flag (available on <code>run</code>, <code>shell</code>, <code>retry</code>, <code>cancel</code>, <code>server start</code>, and <code>docker build</code>).</p>
<p dir="auto">Host ports (<code>host_ports</code>) expose host services to task containers. Agents connect to <code>$TSK_PROXY_HOST:<port></code> to reach services running on your host machine (e.g., local databases or dev servers). The <code>TSK_PROXY_HOST</code> environment variable is automatically set by <code>tsk</code> to the correct proxy container hostname.</p>
<p dir="auto">When <code>git_town</code> is enabled, <code>tsk</code> integrates with <a href="https://www.git-town.com/" rel="nofollow">git-town</a> by setting the parent branch metadata on task branches, allowing git-town commands like <code>git town sync</code> to work correctly with <code>tsk</code>-created branches.</p>
<p dir="auto">Configuration priority: CLI flags > user <code>[project.<name>]</code> > project <code>.tsk/tsk.toml</code> > user <code>[defaults]</code> > auto-detection > built-in defaults</p>
<p dir="auto">Settings in <code>[defaults]</code>, <code>[project.<name>]</code>, and <code>.tsk/tsk.toml</code> share the same shape. Scalars use first-set in priority order. Lists (<code>volumes</code>, <code>env</code>, <code>host_ports</code>) combine across layers, with higher-priority winning on conflicts (same container path, same env var name, same port). <code>stack_config</code>/<code>agent_config</code> maps combine all names; for the same name, higher-priority replaces the entire config.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Customizing the <code>tsk</code> Sandbox Environment</h3><a id="user-content-customizing-the-tsk-sandbox-environment" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Customizing the tsk Sandbox Environment" href="#customizing-the-tsk-sandbox-environment"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Each <code>tsk</code> sandbox container image has 4 main parts:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>A <a href="/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/dockerfiles/base/default.dockerfile">base dockerfile</a> that includes the OS and a set of basic development tools e.g. <code>git</code>, <code>git-lfs</code></li>
<li>A <code>stack</code> snippet that defines language specific build steps. See:
<ul dir="auto">
<li><a href="/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/dockerfiles/stack/default.dockerfile">default</a> - minimal fallback stack</li>
<li><a href="/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/dockerfiles/stack/go.dockerfile">go</a></li>
<li><a href="/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/dockerfiles/stack/java.dockerfile">java</a></li>
<li><a href="/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/dockerfiles/stack/lua.dockerfile">lua</a></li>
<li><a href="/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/dockerfiles/stack/node.dockerfile">node</a></li>
<li><a href="/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/dockerfiles/stack/python.dockerfile">python</a></li>
<li><a href="/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/dockerfiles/stack/rust.dockerfile">rust</a></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>An <code>agent</code> snippet that installs an agent, e.g. <code>claude</code> or <code>codex</code>.</li>
<li>A <code>project</code> snippet that defines project specific build steps (applied last for project-specific customizations). This does nothing by default, but can be used to add extra build steps for your project.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">It is very difficult to make these images general purpose enough to cover all repositories. You may need some special customization. If you use Claude Code, the <code>tsk-config</code> skill can walk you through configuring <code>tsk</code>'s Docker layers for your project (see <a href="#claude-code-skills-marketplace">Claude Code Skills Marketplace</a> for installation). Otherwise, the recommended approach is to use <code>setup</code>, <code>stack_config</code>, and <code>agent_config</code> fields in your <code>tsk.toml</code> to inject custom Dockerfile commands (see <a href="#configuration-file">Configuration File</a> above).</p>
<p dir="auto">See <a href="/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/dockerfiles">dockerfiles</a> for the built-in dockerfiles.</p>
<p dir="auto">You can run <code>tsk docker build --dry-run</code> to see the dockerfile that <code>tsk</code> will dynamically generate for your repository.</p>
<p dir="auto">See the <a href="/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/docs/docker-builds.md">Docker Builds Guide</a> for a more in-depth walk through, and the <a href="/dtormoen/tsk-tsk/blob/main/docs/network-isolation.md">Network Isolation Guide</a> for details on how <code>tsk</code> secures agent network access.</p>
<p dir="auto">I'm working on improving this part of <code>tsk</code> to be as seamless and easy to set up as possible, but it's still a work in progress. I welcome all feedback on how to make this easier and more intuitive!</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Creating Templates</h3><a id="user-content-creating-templates" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Creating Templates" href="#creating-templates"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Templates are simply markdown files that get passed to agents. <code>tsk</code> additionally adds a convenience <code>{{PROMPT}}</code> placeholder that will get replaced by anything you pipe into tsk or pass in via the <code>-p/--prompt</code> flag, or by using <code>--prompt-file <path></code> to read from a file. The legacy <code>{{DESCRIPTION}}</code> placeholder is still supported but deprecated.</p>
<p dir="auto">To inspect an existing template, run <code>tsk template show <template></code>. To customize a built-in template, run <code>tsk template edit <template></code> — <code>tsk</code> will copy it to <code>~/.config/tsk/templates/</code> and open it in your <code>$EDITOR</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">To create good templates, I would recommend thinking about repetitive tasks that you need agents to do within your codebase like "make sure the unit tests pass", "write a commit message", etc. and encode those in a template file. There are many great prompting guides out there so I'll spare the details here.</p>
